clue.text: 12 and 11's what the NHS provides

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a 1938 film starring the two dancers at 12 and 11
second meaning, split in two: medical attention given at no charge

explanation.surface: A boast about Britain's health service and what it hands out.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service, which gives care free at the point of use; read as one word that is a film title.
explanation.definitionFit: The Astaire and Rogers musical of 1938 bears this title, and free care is the health service's founding promise.

clue.text: Disinherit youngster when upper-class humorist, getting a bit of a laugh, came in and died

indicators.note: something that came in has entered, so these pieces go inside the youngster

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, or a novice
a toff is a posh person
a wit is a clever, funny person
abbreviation of Latin obiit, he died

explanation.surface: A posh comedian dies after barging in, and a young heir is cut out of the will.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob is an old British shilling; being left only a shilling was the traditional way of cutting someone out of a will.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means leaving an heir a token shilling, so the phrase describes deliberately excluding someone from an inheritance.

clue.text: Sir Alec was to dance with Madame Peron, also Mr Heath

definitions.note: with 'was', the answer completes the sentence

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: Three politicians, Sir Alec, Evita and Ted Heath, imagined taking to the dance floor together.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Alec Douglas-Home gave up his earldom to become prime minister, then returned to the Lords as a life peer.
explanation.definitionFit: Having renounced one peerage, the former prime minister was later raised to the House of Lords a second time.

clue.text: Went down with a guy

parts.note: fell is the past tense of fall

explanation.surface: Someone tumbled over along with a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are casual informal words for a man or chap.

clue.text: Take the trouble to note reflexes, perhaps

indicators.note: 'perhaps' says the letters only might spell something like this, so a rearrangement is wanted

parts.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor bothering to record a patient's knee-jerk responses.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a real effort or go to some bother over a task is to apply real effort.

clue.text: 12 and 11's — understand? — a debtors' prison

parts.note: to follow an argument is to grasp it
the Fleet was a notorious London prison for debtors

explanation.surface: An aside asking whether the reader grasps a point about an old jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1936 musical film starring the pair of dancers whose names fill 12 and 11.

clue.text: Liftman keeps registered choices for procreation of snails

definitions.note: describes the organ's purpose rather than naming it

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so the inventor's name wraps round the choices

parts.note: Elisha Otis invented the safety elevator

explanation.surface: A lift operator holding on to ballots, oddly linked to snail breeding.
explanation.walkthrough: Otis is the name on many lift doors, hence 'Liftman'.
explanation.definitionFit: This gland of hermaphrodite molluscs produces both eggs and sperm, which is how snails reproduce.

clue.text: The French take little time at the oven

explanation.surface: French cooks spend only a short while at the stove.
explanation.definitionFit: A long furnace used by glassmakers to anneal glass slowly is called by this technical name.

clue.text: T is for Tyler, according to the inventor

parts.note: Wat Tyler led the Peasants' Revolt of 1381
taken as written: the initial standing for the surname

explanation.surface: A spelling-alphabet line attributed to some inventor.
explanation.walkthrough: With T standing for Tyler, Wat Tyler is written Wat T.
explanation.definitionFit: James Watt, the Scottish engineer, developed the improved steam engine and gave his name to the unit of power.

clue.text: See 5
12 and 11's gone to the pub, it doesn''t say where

parts.note: taken as written, 'gone' just sets the scene
PH, public house, is the map abbreviation for a pub
a bare 'at' with no place named after it

explanation.surface: A note left saying someone has gone to the pub, without saying which one.
explanation.walkthrough: The note reads 'gone to PH at' and stops before any place is named.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1935 musical starring the pair of dancers at 12 and 11 carries this title.

clue.text: Dancer and spirit wander in — depart for French department

indicators.note: 'wander in' puts the straying word inside the word for leaving that follows

parts.note: Gers is a department of south-west France

explanation.surface: A dancer, with a drink, strolling about before leaving for a French region.
explanation.definitionFit: The American actress was the famous partner of Fred Astaire in ten musical films.

clue.text: Dancer and journalist held by dreadlocked sectary during shooting

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped inside it, so the journalist sits within the sectary
what happens during an event occurs in the middle of it, so the whole goes inside the shooting

parts.note: ED, editor, the standard crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A dancer and a reporter caught up with a Rastafarian during gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: The journalist goes inside the sectary, and that combination goes inside the shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: The American star was the most celebrated screen hoofer of Hollywood musicals of the 1930s.

clue.text: Engine for crazy poet

explanation.surface: A motor fit for a mad poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Locomotion No 1 was George Stephenson's early railway engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephenson's pioneering steam locomotive of 1825 bore this name, which also means the power of moving.

clue.text: Limited one sort of surgeon — that's by the way

parts.note: Inc, incorporated, is the American equivalent of Ltd
a dental surgeon is a dentist

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain surgeon is narrow-minded, offered as an aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mentioned in passing, as a side issue, is secondary rather than central.

clue.text: Share of punishment?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a portion, as in your fair share

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks about a portion of a penalty, but the two nouns are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the word means a person's portion of money, and also a hard smack given as chastisement.

clue.text: For overhead security the king and I take the limits of Barnaby and his raven

parts.note: K is king in chess notation
R, recipe, Latin for take, heads prescriptions

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its boundaries, its first and last letters only

parts.note: first and last letters of the name
Grip is the raven in Dickens's Barnaby Rudge

explanation.surface: A king and his companion seizing hold of Barnaby Rudge and his bird.
explanation.walkthrough: A kirby grip is a British name for a sprung hairpin, what Americans call a bobby pin.
explanation.definitionFit: This small sprung hairpin holds hair in place on the head, keeping it secure.

clue.text: Pole with gong hiding among the bedclothes?

definitions.note: describes the answer as one of the things worn in bed

indicators.note: a hiding is a thrashing, and the beaten letters end up knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone with a medal tucked away under the covers.
explanation.walkthrough: A gong is British slang for a medal, but here the word supplies only letters, and 'with' joins them in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose garment worn for sleeping counts as one of the clothes you wear to bed.

clue.text: Person of ideas: the alternative is HM

explanation.surface: A thinker being offered the Queen as the other option.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who forms speculative explanations and hypotheses is a thinker dealing in concepts.

clue.text: All about nothing with one to finish, as they say

definitions.note: what the Finns themselves call their country

indicators.note: placing a piece to finish means it goes at the very end of the build
about means around, so the word for all goes round the nothing

parts.note: the sum is the whole lot

explanation.surface: A fuss about nothing, with someone needed to wrap it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To finish' places the one at the end, and also puns on Finnish: 'they' are the Finns, saying the name of their country.
explanation.definitionFit: Finland's native name in the Finnish language is this word, so it is what the inhabitants call it.

clue.text: Possibly Jasper National Park

definitions.meaning: first meaning: jasper is a gem that can be a golden colour
second meaning: the famous American park of Wyoming

explanation.walkthrough: Jasper National Park is real, in Canada, so the clue looks like a single name; split it after Jasper.
explanation.definitionFit: Jasper is a quartz gem sometimes golden in colour, and the oldest US national park bears this name.

clue.text: 12 and 11's second side on the clock?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a 1936 film starring the dancers at 12 and 11

definitions.note: a cryptic hint rather than a dictionary sense
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a pendulum moving across to the other side each second

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second meaning: a clock's pendulum takes a set period to move from one side to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1936 Astaire and Rogers musical has this title, and a pendulum's period of oscillation fits the playful reading.

clue.text: See 1
See 21
Richard's pipes?

definitions.note: the surname of a Richard, not a possessive
definitions.meaning: first meaning: Richard ..., English actor of The Good Life
second meaning: tobacco pipes carved from brier root

explanation.walkthrough: The clue seems to ask about one man's pipes; the actor's surname and the pipes are two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Briers was a much-loved British comic actor, and smoking pipes are often made of heath root wood.

clue.text: Champion of women has Tracey in hand

indicators.note: the artist is in the hand, so her name sits inside the word for a hand

parts.note: a fist is a clenched hand

explanation.surface: A women's advocate who has the artist Tracey Emin under control.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who advocates equal rights for the female sex campaigns on their behalf.

clue.text: Electronically summons student among similar sounds

indicators.note: being among things means placed in their midst, so the student goes inside the sounds

parts.note: beeps are sounds like the ones a pager makes

explanation.surface: A pager calling a student amid a chorus of similar noises.
explanation.definitionFit: Paging someone, such as a doctor, by a pocket device that emits a tone is to call them.

clue.text: Islands disturbing lagoon where magnetic is not true

definitions.note: describes the lines rather than naming them

indicators.note: disturbing something churns it up, so the letters of the water are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Islands churning up a lagoon at a spot where compasses mislead.
explanation.definitionFit: Isogonal lines join places of equal magnetic declination, the angle by which compass north differs from geographic north.
